tldr: InfoDeepSeek is a new benchmark with 245 challenging, human-validated questions and a fine-grained evaluation framework designed to assess agentic information seeking in real-world, dynamic web environments, addressing the limitations of existing static RAG benchmarks.
contributions: Introduction of criteria and a systematic methodology for constructing challenging queries, plus the InfoDeepSeek benchmark covering 14 domains and 19 predominant languages
Proposal of an Agentic RAG framework coupled with the first fine-grained evaluation metrics and protocols that assess information seeking effectiveness in dynamic environments
Comprehensive comparison of agents across different LLMs, search engines, and question types, revealing agent behaviors and limitations with actionable insights for future research
methods: The authors manually curated and validated 245 high-quality questions designed to satisfy criteria of determinacy, difficulty, and diversity, with attributes including multi-hop reasoning (76.73%), long-tail knowledge (77.14%), time-sensitive content (66.12%), freshness requirements (19.59%), distracting information (31.02%), and false premises (10.61%). They developed an Agentic RAG system that integrates multiple search and browsing tools (Google, Bing, Yahoo, DuckDuckGo, Selenium) in live web environments, supporting up to 5 retrieval steps and evidence sets of up to 5 documents. They proposed four evaluation metrics—Answer Accuracy (ACC), Information Accuracy at k (IA@k), Effective Evidence Utilization (EEU), and Information Compactness (IC)—to assess agents' information seeking capabilities beyond simple answer correctness.
results: The paper reports conducting extensive experiments across multiple LLMs, search engines, and question types, revealing nuanced agent behaviors and offering actionable insights for future research. The benchmark covers 14 domains and 19 predominant languages. A mitigation strategy for LLM-based evaluation of false premise questions improved evaluation accuracy from 95.57% to 99.29% compared to human evaluation. Specific numerical results from the experiments are truncated in the provided text.
limitations: Existing RAG benchmarks are confined to static retrieval environments with fixed, limited corpora that fail to reflect the scale and dynamics of real-world web environments. Their evaluation protocols rely on pre-defined ground-truth documents and metrics like NDCG, which are unsuitable for the open-ended nature of dynamic web settings. Additionally, existing benchmarks use simple queries that cannot elicit core agentic behaviors such as planning, multi-turn tool use, and reasoning over multiple pieces of evidence. The paper also notes that LLM evaluators commonly fail to identify incorrect assumptions in false premise questions without explicit mitigation strategies.
